description: We are Bananaut, a team exploring how the Nile island between Shorbas and Al-Sawalem in Damietta, Egypt, has changed over time. For the Earth System Trend Detective challenge, we plan to use NASA satellite data to track shoreline and vegetation changes and build an interactive tool that shows where changes are happening, how large they are, and whether they reflect a long-term trend. We welcome teammates interested in mapping, data analysis, and web development.
summary:
A single satellite image can show how green a field is on one day, but it cannot tell us whether vegetation is changing over time. Project Bananaut is an interactive dashboard that helps users explore how vegetation greenness changed on Shorbas Island, Egypt, from 2018 to 2025.

We used satellite imagery from NASA’s Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) dataset to calculate the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), a measure of vegetation greenness. We excluded cloud and cloud-shadow pixels and compared observations from the same seasonal window across years to reduce the influence of seasonal differences. The dashboard lets users select a range of years and see how greenness changed over that period.

By turning satellite observations into an easy-to-read comparison, Bananaut helps users spot changes worth investigating without assuming that the satellite data alone can explain what caused them.
details:
Bananaut is an interactive web dashboard that helps users compare vegetation greenness on Shorbas Island, Egypt, from 2018 to 2025. It addresses the “Be an Earth System Trend Detective” challenge by turning satellite observations into a time series that users can explore.

We used NASA’s Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) data and processed the satellite imagery in Python. We used the red and near-infrared bands to calculate the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), filtered out pixels flagged as clouds or cloud shadows, and summarized the remaining observations by year. We compared observations from the same seasonal window to reduce the influence of seasonal differences.

The dashboard lets users select a range of years and compare NDVI values over time. This makes a large satellite dataset easier to explore and helps users identify changes worth investigating. A change in NDVI indicates a difference in observed vegetation greenness, but it does not by itself reveal what caused the change or measure crop yield.
